case_name: L. O. v. Mt. Lebanon S.D.

issues.label: Standard of review of Board adjudication
issues.why: The court must determine whether common pleas and it apply the correct scope/standard when reviewing a local agency adjudication.

issues.label: Whether common pleas exceeded review authority
issues.why: Common pleas may have improperly substituted its own findings or reweighed evidence rather than reviewing for substantial evidence and legal error.

issues.label: Legal definition of residency under Section 1302
issues.why: The court must interpret what 'reside' means—physical presence versus domicile or primary residence—for school enrollment.

issues.label: Physical presence versus domicile standard
issues.why: The parties dispute whether mere physical presence suffices or whether a higher domicile/primary residence showing is required.

issues.label: Whether residency in two districts is permissible
issues.why: The District argues Section 1302 cannot allow a parent to be resident of multiple districts simultaneously.

issues.label: Allocation and shifting of burden of proof
issues.why: The court must decide who bore the burden and whether it shifted from Mother to the District.

issues.label: Waiver of District's newly-raised arguments
issues.why: Mother contends burden-of-proof and multiple-district arguments were raised for the first time on appeal and thus waived.

issues.label: Substantial evidence supporting non-residency finding
issues.why: The court must assess whether returned mail, low utility usage, and surveillance constitute substantial evidence of non-residency.

issues.label: Deference to Board credibility determinations
issues.why: The court must decide whether common pleas improperly rejected the Board's credibility findings on Mother and the Service Provider.

issues.label: Sufficiency of overnight stays for residency
issues.why: Whether 10 of 36 nights (roughly one-third) establishes physical presence is a mixed law-fact question central to the dispute.

issues.label: Relevant time period for residency assessment
issues.why: Dispute over whether residency is measured from lease signing, key receipt (Oct 20), or across the whole school year.

issues.label: Effect of intent versus actual residence
issues.why: The court must address whether Mother's stated desire to live in the District bears on the residency determination.

issues.label: Weight of Mother's admissions
issues.why: The Adjudication rested heavily on Mother's admissions about nights stayed and lack of access.

issues.label: Explanations for absences from apartment
issues.why: The court must weigh whether illness, oral surgery, and unlivable conditions excuse observed absences.

issues.label: Denial of after-discovered evidence hearing
issues.why: The District challenges denial of a hearing to present later video surveillance evidence.

issues.label: Limitation of record and supplemental reproduced record
issues.why: The District contends common pleas improperly accepted a supplemental record after ruling the record complete.

issues.label: Judicial notice of Residency/Enrollment Policy
issues.why: Mother argues the 60-day notice policy is a public record reviewable via judicial notice despite not being considered below.

issues.label: District compliance with own notice policy
issues.why: Whether the District's alleged failure to give 60 school days' notice invalidates its non-residency determination.

issues.label: Propriety of investigation and surveillance methods
issues.why: The limited scope and reliability of the District's surveillance may affect evidentiary weight and due process.

issues.label: Scope of tuition liability for full year
issues.why: Mother disputes imposing full-year tuition without regard to possible residency changes after the hearing.

issues.label: Interpretation of ambiguous documentary evidence
issues.why: Lease, driver's license, insurance, electric bill, and mailing addresses point in conflicting directions requiring reconciliation.

issues.label: Applicability of separated-parents rules
issues.why: The Board found no separated-parents issue despite estranged co-ownership of the Pittsburgh House, which may affect residency analysis.

issues.label: Due process at the residency hearing
issues.why: The court should ensure Mother received adequate notice and opportunity to be heard before losing tuition-free status.
